cases.name: invoice_totals
cases.reason: Joins invoice headers, customers, and lines while keeping join and grouping columns as reads and line values as output lineage.
cases.sql: SELECT i.InvoiceId AS invoice_id, c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS customer_name, SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS line_total FROM Invoice AS i JOIN Customer AS c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId JOIN InvoiceLine AS il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId GROUP BY i.InvoiceId, c.FirstName, c.LastName HAVING SUM(il.Quantity) > 0 ORDER BY i.InvoiceId

cases.name: support_rep_sales
cases.reason: Groups invoice revenue by employee through customer support assignments and uses COUNT(*) as a source-free row count.
cases.sql: SELECT e.EmployeeId AS employee_id, e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS rep_name, COUNT(*) AS invoice_count, SUM(i.Total) AS revenue FROM Employee AS e JOIN Customer AS c ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId JOIN Invoice AS i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName HAVING SUM(i.Total) > 0 ORDER BY revenue DESC, rep_name

cases.name: employee_hierarchy
cases.reason: Self-joins employees to report manager and report names while the ReportsTo predicate remains a read-only dependency.
cases.sql: SELECT manager.EmployeeId AS manager_id, manager.FirstName || ' ' || manager.LastName AS manager_name, report.EmployeeId AS report_id, report.FirstName || ' ' || report.LastName AS report_name FROM Employee AS manager JOIN Employee AS report ON report.ReportsTo = manager.EmployeeId WHERE report.EmployeeId IS NOT NULL ORDER BY manager.LastName, report.LastName

cases.name: track_wildcard
cases.reason: Expands a table wildcard into every Track column while the filter and ordering reuse columns already covered by that expansion.
cases.sql: SELECT t.* FROM Track AS t WHERE t.GenreId IS NOT NULL AND t.UnitPrice >= 0.99 ORDER BY t.Name

cases.name: monthly_invoice_revenue
cases.reason: Normalizes invoice dates in a CTE and aggregates invoice totals by the derived month value.
cases.sql: WITH invoice_month AS (SELECT substr(i.InvoiceDate, 1, 7) AS invoice_month, i.Total AS invoice_total FROM Invoice AS i) SELECT invoice_month AS month, SUM(invoice_total) AS revenue FROM invoice_month GROUP BY invoice_month HAVING SUM(invoice_total) > 0 ORDER BY month

cases.name: top_album_sales
cases.reason: Aggregates track sales in a derived table, then joins the result to album titles for a reporting ranking.
cases.sql: SELECT a.Title AS album_title, sales.track_count, sales.revenue FROM Album AS a JOIN (SELECT t.AlbumId AS album_id, COUNT(il.InvoiceLineId) AS track_count, SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS revenue FROM Track AS t JOIN InvoiceLine AS il ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId GROUP BY t.AlbumId) AS sales ON sales.album_id = a.AlbumId WHERE sales.revenue > 10 ORDER BY sales.revenue DESC, album_title

cases.name: customer_lifetime_value
cases.reason: Uses correlated scalar subqueries to compute each customer's invoice total and retain only customers with invoices.
cases.sql: SELECT c.CustomerId AS customer_id, c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS customer_name, (SELECT SUM(i.Total) FROM Invoice AS i WHERE i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId) AS lifetime_value FROM Customer AS c WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Invoice AS i WHERE i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId) > 0 ORDER BY lifetime_value DESC

cases.name: engaged_customers
cases.reason: Filters customers with a qualifying invoice and excludes customers sharing the same support representative.
cases.sql: SELECT c.CustomerId AS customer_id, c.Email AS email FROM Customer AS c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Invoice AS i WHERE i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId AND i.Total >= 20) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Customer AS c2 WHERE c2.SupportRepId = c.SupportRepId AND c2.CustomerId <> c.CustomerId) ORDER BY c.Email

cases.name: playlist_or_premium_tracks
cases.reason: Unions playlist membership with premium invoice lines, preserving both track-id sources and the shared track name source.
cases.sql: SELECT pt.TrackId AS track_id, t.Name AS track_name FROM PlaylistTrack AS pt JOIN Track AS t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId UNION SELECT il.TrackId AS track_id, t.Name AS track_name FROM InvoiceLine AS il JOIN Track AS t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId WHERE il.UnitPrice >= 0.99

cases.name: customers_without_recent_invoices
cases.reason: Uses EXCEPT to report customer rows absent from the recent-invoice set; right-side columns affect membership only.
cases.sql: SELECT c.CustomerId AS customer_id, c.Email AS email FROM Customer AS c EXCEPT SELECT c.CustomerId, c.Email FROM Customer AS c JOIN Invoice AS i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId WHERE i.InvoiceDate >= '2023-01-01' ORDER BY email

cases.name: long_rock_tracks
cases.reason: Returns only the track name while duration, genre, price, and ordering predicates remain read dependencies.
cases.sql: SELECT t.Name AS track_name FROM Track AS t WHERE t.Milliseconds >= 300000 AND t.GenreId IN (1, 3, 13) AND t.UnitPrice < 1.00 ORDER BY t.Milliseconds DESC

cases.name: left_using
cases.sql: SELECT CustomerId AS id FROM Invoice LEFT JOIN Customer USING (CustomerId)
cases.reason: LEFT/RIGHT USING returns the preserved key; FULL coalesces both. Both keys remain join reads.

cases.name: right_using
cases.sql: SELECT CustomerId AS id FROM Invoice RIGHT JOIN Customer USING (CustomerId)
cases.reason: LEFT/RIGHT USING returns the preserved key; FULL coalesces both. Both keys remain join reads.

cases.name: full_using
cases.sql: SELECT CustomerId AS id FROM Invoice FULL JOIN Customer USING (CustomerId)
cases.reason: LEFT/RIGHT USING returns the preserved key; FULL coalesces both. Both keys remain join reads.

cases.name: derived_alias_star
cases.sql: SELECT report.* FROM (SELECT InvoiceId AS sale, Total AS amount FROM Invoice) report
cases.reason: Wildcard expansion preserves derived output aliases instead of replacing them with physical source column names.
